snippet.description:
Explore the promise and perils of new A.I. technologies.

Official Website: https://to.pbs.org/3Py2WDL | #novapbs 

Can we harness the power of artificial intelligence to solve the world’s most challenging problems without creating an uncontrollable force that ultimately destroys us? ChatGPT and other new A.I. tools can now answer complex questions, write essays, and generate realistic-looking images in a matter of seconds. They can even pass a lawyer’s bar exam. Should we celebrate? Or worry? Or both? Correspondent Miles O’Brien investigates how researchers are trying to transform the world using A.I., hunting for big solutions in fields from medicine to climate change.

✔ New career opportunities created by AI

Companies have been trying to cut down on workers for as long as those workers have demanded pay and benefits. 

Whether it’s downsizing, outsourcing, streamlining, understaffing, or automating, if there is something a business can do to get rid of workers and their salaries, you better believe they are going to do it. 

But this time does feel a little bit different. Recent AI advances have been mocked for not quiet living up to the bold claims of their tech bro founders. 

But even in their current, imperfect form, LLM’s, general use robots and generative models are ALREADY replacing jobs and they are getting better every day.

So that’s bad for workers, but if you are a senior corporate executive or company owner, maybe you should be asking yourself…

If we automate everybody’s job… who is going to buy all of your stuff? 

I have some good news and some bad news for your theoretical company. 

The good news is that labor reduction systems of all varieties have ALREADY cut out millions of manhours in America alone and made the workers who are left more efficient at their jobs. 

Artificial intelligence is just another tool that your company can use to get more work out of fewer staff or replace teams entirely. 

Even here at little old works media group we used to have someone working part time whose job it was just to cut out images on Photoshop to use in our goofy little animations.

Applying for jobs is tough. 

Click here to subscribe to our channel 👉🏽 https://bbc.in/3VyyriM

snippet.title: This is how Ai steals your job? (Short Documentary)
snippet.description:
Will an AI steal your job in near future?

Will an AI steal your job
Perhaps a more realistic near-future prospect is that artificially intelligent technologies will replace most of present physical labour.
While AI will not replace all professions, it appears that AI will transform the nature of labour, with the main issue being how quickly and deeply automation will impact the workplace.
There isn't a single sector of human endeavour where AI hasn't had an influence. As Andrew Ng, an AI scientist puts it: "Many individuals work in normal, repetitive tasks. Unfortunately, technology is extremely adept at automating regular, repetitive labour," he says, predicting a "substantial danger of technological unemployment in the next decades."
Evidence of which jobs will be displaced is beginning to surface. In the United States, there are currently 27 Amazon Go shops and cashier-free supermarkets where consumers may just pick things from the shelves and walk out. What this implies for the more than three million cashiers in the United States remains to be seen. Amazon is once again setting the standard for employing robots to increase warehouse productivity. These robots transport product shelves to human pickers, who choose which goods to send out. Amazon already employs around 200000 bots in its fulfilment centres, with plans to add more in the future. However, Amazon emphasises that as the number of bots has increased, so has the number of human workers at these warehouses.
Although truly automated self-driving cars are not yet a reality, some anticipate that the self-driving trucks industry alone would eliminate over 1.7 million jobs over the next decade, even before accounting for the impact on couriers and taxi drivers.
However, some of the simplest activities to automate will not even necessitate the use of robotics. At the moment, millions of people work in administration, inputting and transferring data across systems, pursuing and making meetings for businesses. However, as software improves at automatically updating systems and marking vital information, the need for administrators will diminish.
As with each technological development, new employment will be created to compensate for those that are lost. However, it is unclear if these new positions will be established quickly enough to hire people who have been laid off, and whether the newly jobless will have the required skills or temperament to fill these growing roles.
Everyone is not a pessimist. For some, artificial intelligence is a technology that will complement rather than replace workers. Not only that, but they argue that there will be a commercial imperative not to completely replace people, because an AI-assisted worker – imagine a human concierge with an AR headset that tells them exactly what a client wants before they ask for it – will be more productive or effective than an AI working alone.
Among AI specialists, there is a wide variety of ideas on how rapidly artificially intelligent systems will surpass human skills.
The Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford University asked several hundred machine-learning professionals to forecast AI capabilities over the next few decades.
Notable dates include AI authoring essays that might pass for human writing by 2026, truck drivers being replaced by 2027, AI surpassing human skills in retail by 2031, writing a best-seller by 2049, and performing surgical procedures by 2053.
They anticipated that AI will outperform humans in all tasks within 45 years and automate all human employment by 120 years.

What this implies for the more than three million cashiers in the United States remains to be seen. Amazon is once again setting the standard for employing robots to increase warehouse productivity. These robots transport product shelves to human pickers, who choose which goods to send out. Amazon already employs around 200000 bots in its fulfilment centres, with plans to add more in the future. However, Amazon emphasises that as the number of bots has increased, so has the number of human workers at these warehouses.
Although truly automated self-driving cars are not yet a reality, some anticipate that the self-driving trucks industry alone would eliminate over 1.7 million jobs over the next decade, even before accounting for the impact on couriers and taxi drivers.
However, some of the simplest activities to automate will not even necessitate the use of robotics. At the moment, millions of people work in administration, inputting and transferring data across systems, pursuing and making meetings for businesses. However, as software improves at automatically updating systems and marking vital information, the need for administrators will diminish.
As with each technological development, new employment will be created to compensate for those that are lost. However, it is unclear if these new positions will be established quickly enough to hire people who have been laid off, and whether the newly jobless will have the required skills or temperament to fill these growing roles.
Everyone is not a pessimist. For some, artificial intelligence is a technology that will complement rather than replace workers. Not only that, but they argue that there will be a commercial imperative not to completely replace people, because an AI-assisted worker – imagine a human concierge with an AR headset that tells them exactly what a client wants before they ask for it – will be more productive or effective than an AI working alone.
Among AI specialists, there is a wide variety of ideas on how rapidly artificially intelligent systems will surpass human skills.
The Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford University asked several hundred machine-learning professionals to forecast AI capabilities over the next few decades.
Notable dates include AI authoring essays that might pass for human writing by 2026, truck drivers being replaced by 2027, AI surpassing human skills in retail by 2031, writing a best-seller by 2049, and performing surgical procedures by 2053.
They anticipated that AI will outperform humans in all tasks within 45 years and automate all human employment by 120 years.
